claims.statement: The `scheduler` assistant is a single-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered in langgraph.json; its `_launch` node deterministically routes each tick to one handler and does not use an LLM.

Scheduler task routing handles reconciliation, baby-sit watches, background tasks, workspace refreshes, session and agent cost refreshes, thread feedback, and human-review deadlines; a tick without a recognized task launches a stored automation schedule.
Missing keyed scheduler inputs return explicit missing statuses, and exhausted transient sandbox-attach failures return `sandbox_unavailable` instead of failing the scheduler invocation.
Automation schedule triggers validate normalized five-field cron expressions with field-specific ranges and support numeric values, wildcards, ranges, steps, and lists.

Automations are stored in PostgreSQL as automation and automation_trigger records; each schedule trigger owns a LangGraph cron, while GitHub-trigger deliveries are claimed once per automation before launch.
`reconcile_stale_runs` pages through busy threads and interrupts pending runs older than the default 1,800 seconds, preventing lost completion webhooks from holding threads busy indefinitely.
The reconciliation sweep isolates per-thread failures, skips unparseable timestamps, and returns counts for threads checked, stale runs, and cancellations.

Session-cost refresh is a bounded chain of stateless delayed scheduler runs using five fixed delays and `on_completion="delete"`; only a pending refresh schedules another attempt, while unavailable and exhausted outcomes terminate and clear the pending marker.

A BabySitWatch is persisted under a lower-cased owner/repo#PR key and binds an agent thread, PR head, GitHub App installation, follow-up configuration, source context, retry and deduplication state, evaluation errors, and cron identity.
Only one active agent thread may watch a pull request; restarting on the same head carries retry and deduplication state, while a new head starts that state over.

Starting a baby-sit watch idempotently reuses or creates a ten-minute scheduler cron and removes duplicates; failure to create a cron for a brand-new watch rolls back its stored row and known partial cron.

The GitHub webhook route rejects requests without a valid X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC, and baby-sit handles completed CI payloads by matching active repository watches by head SHA or branch and deduplicating delivery IDs before evaluation.
Baby-sit cron and webhook evaluation both use a five-minute per-watch LangGraph-thread lock, so a concurrent evaluation returns busy rather than dispatching the same failure twice.

A changed baby-sit PR head resets retries and failure/alert dedupe state; a new failure stores a SHA-and-retry fingerprint before enqueuing an untrusted-signal diagnostic follow-up, and removes that fingerprint if dispatch fails.

Flaky reruns are capped at three per PR head; `record_retry` requires ownership and matching head SHA, durably increments the retry count, and posts a flaky-CI alert only once for a head/check/safe GitHub URL combination.

Baby-sit stops closed PRs and terminal outcomes; ready checks enqueue a follow-up to the origin thread, while other terminal outcomes attempt source notification and fall back to an enqueued `/baby-sit --terminal` run before stopping the watch.

The `manage_baby_sit` tool requires a canonical GitHub PR URL and executable thread, verifies authentication and an open PR before starting, and restricts stop and retry operations to the owning thread.

Background-task completion is callback-first for opted-in launches and otherwise uses an idempotent per-thread every-minute scheduler cron; terminal tasks are atomically claimed, enqueued to their owning thread, and marked delivered only after dispatch succeeds.

`schedule_thread_wakeup` creates a thread-bound one-shot cron for the `agent` assistant with a delay from one minute to 24 hours, a UTC fire time rounded to a minute, and an end time 90 seconds after firing.
Thread wakeups are limited to ten per latest human-message generation; the generation and count are held in thread metadata, reset by a new human message, and recorded before cron creation.
Wakeup cron rows remain after firing, so wakeup scheduling best-effort purges only fully paginated `thread_wakeup` crons whose end_time has passed; explicit thread cleanup is also available.

Agent-cost refresh fetches a run-only LangSmith cost, persists it to invocation usage and thread metadata, and retries retrieval or persistence failures through the same five-delay budget before terminating.
Focused tests cover scheduler routing, baby-sit deduplication and locking, required-check progression, terminal fallback, retry caps, head resets, stale-run reconciliation, and wakeup behavior.

When a schedule cron fires, `launch_scheduled_agent_run` verifies the stored automation and its fired schedule trigger, removes orphan crons for missing or replaced definitions, and launches only a matching automation record.
A background-task polling monitor removes its crons when no work remains only after acquiring a sandbox monitor lock and rechecking task state, avoiding deletion during a concurrent transition.

Baby-sit success requires acceptable observed checks and all required branch checks to be reported; incomplete, absent, or unreported required checks remain pending, while other terminal non-success states are blocked for triage.
